text:
zoe: console shows a sudden p95 bump for /v1/chat at 14:07. drill-down shows a tiny 'router-fallback' cohort (count=9) — merged p95 is 210ms but main client cohort p95 is 34ms.

eli: classic small-cohort tail domination. we should surface sample_count next to percentiles and dim percentiles with low confidence.

marc: backend note: merged percentile must be computed from raw samples or merged sketch; do NOT approximate by weighting per-cohort p95s.

courtney: UX: add a small "confidence" pill (green/yellow/red) based on sample_count and ci width; tooltip explains "small cohorts can skew tail percentiles".

eli: API change idea: /metrics/percentiles?endpoint=/v1/chat&include_cohorts=true&min_count=50 returning rows like ["cohort","p95","count"]. keep everything stringified for the console.

marc: also compute delta_if_removed for top cohorts so we can show which cohort moves merged p95 the most if excluded. useful for triage.

ops-bot: deploybot: routing-fallback-rollout 2025-06-20T14:00:00Z deployed (staging 30%). linked to #routing.

zoe: ok will open a small ticket linking the routing rollout and request design mock + API. goal: reduce false alarms and speed triage.
